title: Make room
hook: when told to make room in assemblies, make room, and Allah makes room for you (58:11)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-Mujadila, she who pleads her case, and your line, she was heard.

A crowded table at a family dinner. Someone arrives late, plate in hand, and stands there. Everyone is mid-conversation. Nobody moves. The latecomer hovers, then drifts to the kitchen counter to eat alone. It takes one person to say, here, squeeze in, and shift their chair six inches. Six inches, and someone belongs. Surah Al-Mujadila has a verse about that moment, set in the gatherings around the Prophet ﷺ in Medina, and it comes with a promise attached.

Verse eleven. Pickthall: "O ye who believe! when it is said, Make room! in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make way for you (hereafter)." The verb is tafassahu, make space, spread out, from the root f-s-h, wideness, roominess. Commentators report the setting: people sat close around the Prophet, and some latecomers, among them men who had fought at Badr, were left standing, because those seated didn't want to give up their places near him. The verse answers: make room. And notice the trade. You give up a few inches, and God makes room for you. Commentators read that widely: room in the grave, in paradise, in your life and your heart, in your provision. The verse continues: when you're told to rise, rise; God will raise those of you who believe, and those given knowledge, by degrees. Hadith fill in the manners. Bukhari and Muslim record that the Prophet said no one should make another person get up from his seat so that he can sit there. Instead, spread out and make room. So the rule cuts both ways. The one sitting should shift and make space. The one arriving shouldn't push anyone out. Between them, a crowded room gets bigger without a single chair added. In this verse, space isn't only something you have. It's something people make for each other.

segments.voice: Notice how much room you take up right now, arms, legs, bag, and on an out-breath shift slightly, as if leaving a space beside you. Then think of one person standing at the edge of something, a new coworker, a quiet cousin, a neighbor, and picture moving your chair six inches for them.
Make room. When told to make room in gatherings, make room, and God will make room for you. Today's word.
Your line: squeeze in, shift six inches. The verse promises room in return. That's day six hundred seventeen.

howItsDone: In mosques and gatherings, Muslims are taught to close up and make room for newcomers, especially in the rows of prayer and at the Friday sermon, and not to make anyone rise from their seat.

what a scholar hears: tafassahu from f-s-h; the occasion reported with the people of Badr; 'yafsahi llahu lakum' read broadly; Bukhari 6270 and Muslim 2177 on not raising anyone from his seat.

chat.says: If a gathering is full, should I ask someone to give me their seat?
options: No, the hadith says don't make anyone get up; those seated should spread out.
Yes, latecomers always get first pick of the seats near the speaker.
Yes, whoever is closest to the speaker should give up their place.
chat.meaning: Bukhari and Muslim: no one should make another get up to take his seat. Instead, spread out, as 58:11 says: make room.
